headline: Open-source 3D-printed portable MRI machine built for under $70,000
summary: This DIY medical equipment costs less than 7% of a full-sized MRI machine's $1.1 million starting price. AI can enhance its lower resolution for medical diagnoses.
details: A new open-source, 3D-printed portable MRI machine, the OSI2 ONE, has been developed for under $70,000. This significantly reduces the cost compared to full-sized MRI units, which start at $1.1 million and can exceed $3 million.

The OSI2 ONE has a limited field strength of 50mT, much lower than the 1.5T to 3T of standard units, resulting in lower spatial resolution and signal-to-noise ratio. However, tech analyst Brian Roemmele suggests that modern AI can overcome these limitations for medical diagnoses.

AI models, specially trained on high-field MRI data or physics-informed models, can denoise images, correct for inhomogeneity, and push resolution beyond raw acquisition limits. Real-time sequence adaptation can also adjust gradients and RF pulses as AI monitors signal quality.

Institutions without access to anonymized patient data for training specialized AI can use synthetic data generation, leveraging the open-source nature of the OSI2 ONE scanner. This allows researchers to build physics models for AI training.

While regulatory hurdles exist in first-world countries, the project is particularly impactful for regions with limited access to expensive medical technologies. Even refurbished MRI machines cost over $100,000, plus significant setup expenses.

Though a portable MRI may not match the resolution of full-sized machines, its affordability, combined with effective AI enhancement, makes it a vital tool. This innovation could provide life-saving diagnostic access to less wealthy hospitals and clinics globally.

headline_marked: [[Terax packs a terminal, editor, git, and AI agent]] into an 8 MB binary
headline: Terax packs a terminal, editor, git, and AI agent into an 8 MB binary
summary: Terax combines a full terminal, code editor, git client with a commit graph, web preview, and an agentic AI panel into a single 8 MB application. It's built on Tauri 2 and Rust for a lightweight, account-free, and telemetry-free developer workspace.
details: Terax is a comprehensive dev environment, fitting a terminal, editor, git client, web preview, and AI agent into an 8 MB binary. It achieves this compact size by leveraging Tauri 2 and Rust, avoiding a heavy bundled browser runtime. The application requires no account and sends no telemetry.

The core is its terminal, built on xterm.js with a WebGL renderer and a native PTY backend. It supports various shells like zsh, bash, and pwsh, offering features like split panels, inline search, and true color. On Windows, it provides first-class WSL integration, allowing different workspace environments per tab.

The integrated editor, powered by CodeMirror 6, includes Vim mode and ten themes. Its source control panel features individual hunk staging, commit functionality, upstream-aware pushing, and a history pane with an actual commit graph. A file explorer with fuzzy search and inline rename, plus a web preview pane, are also built-in.

Terax's AI capabilities are central, supporting bring-your-own-key integration with major providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and Groq. Crucially, it also supports fully local inference via LM Studio, MLX, and Ollama, ensuring code privacy. Inline autocomplete also works with local models.

The AI agent goes beyond simple chat, planning multi-step tasks, spawning sub-agents, and maintaining project memory in a TERAX.md file. It comes with a robust toolset for file operations (read, write, edit, grep, glob) and bash execution, with approval gating. Users can define custom agents and accept/reject code edits hunk by hunk.

Credentials like API keys are securely stored in the OS keychain, never touching disk or localStorage. While still early in development and not yet code-signed on Windows, Terax offers auto-updates and is available for Arch and Nix users.

Its technical foundation includes Tauri 2, Rust, portable-pty, React 19, TypeScript, xterm.js, CodeMirror 6, and Vercel AI SDK v6. Terax targets developers seeking an agentic coding setup without a heavy footprint, mandatory login, or telemetry.
